text:
elaine: Heads-up — seeing a sharp p95/p99 spike on hosted API starting ~2026-03-19T09:14Z. Short-sequence requests (<32 tokens) p95 ~420ms -> ~950ms, p99 ~800ms -> ~2.1s. Looks sudden and tenanty.
grafana-bot: link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/hosted/p95-heat?from=2026-03-19T09:00Z&to=2026-03-19T09:30Z
marcus: A few quick checks: is this correlated with kernel selector flips? short seqs can cause sampler to prefer aux kernel which spikes latency. Pulling selector logs.
elaine: selector logs show ~09:13:58 a burst of short requests mapping to kernel_aux for a subset of hosts. Also queue depth on queue-frontend rose from 2 -> 12.
nina: attaching miniature flame from one affected host (trimmed):
```
flame: runtimes:kernel_aux 45% | kernel_primary 12% | gc 3% | user 40%
hot path: kvcache.lookup -> batcher.coalesce -> kernel_exec(aux): high memcpy
```
marcus: memcpy on aux kernel indicates small-batch codepath is hitting a non-optimal kernel (no fused attention). Likely due to batcher heuristics flipping from coalesced to eager small batches.
tom: Any deploys around that time? Could be a change in batching config we rolled out.
deploy-bot: rollout: batching-config-v2 deployed @ 2026-03-19T08:58Z to rollout group=hosted-frontends (50%).
elaine: that matches. Also tenant acme-analytics spiked QPS from 120 -> 900 sustained for ~5m starting 09:13. Their traffic is almost all short messages (analytics pings).
marcus: hypothesis: rollout made sampler more aggressive for low-latency preferring small batches, causing kernel_aux to be chosen and queue depth to climb (backpressure) when tenant spikes -> tail latencies.
nina: did a quick trace of kvcache: miss ratio up ~16% -> 38% for those seqs. Prefetch thrash on short sequences means more priming work -> aux kernel overhead dominates.
elaine: mitigation idea 1: throttle tenant to reduce thundering small requests. Idea 2: pin kernel selector to prefer primary kernel for short seqs until we get more profiling. Idea 3: rollback batching-config-v2. Thoughts?
tom: throttle acme-analytics by applying rate bucket cap at edge for 5m. We have a fast path in rateengine to cap by tenant.
marcus: prefer pin+targeted throttle. Rolling back rollout is heavier and affects many tenants. I'll push a selector pin to hosted-frontends that forces kernel_primary for seq<=32 on canary hosts.
elaine: I can apply tenant throttle now. Applying acme-analytics cap -> 200 RPS.
sre-rotation: ack, monitoring p95.
(grafana-bot posts updated graph)
grafana-bot: p95 graph updated: before mitigation peak ~950ms, 60s after throttle: ~210ms. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/hosted/p95-heat?from=2026-03-19T09:10Z&to=2026-03-19T09:40Z
marcus: selector pin rolled to 50% of hosted-frontends at 09:20. Observed kernel_aux % drop from 68% -> 22% on pinned hosts.
nina: running a small profiler on pinned hosts shows memcpy cost down 3x; kvcache miss trend still high for acme but overall tail improved.
tom: we left batching-config-v2 rollout paused. Ops: keep rollout paused until we do perf A/B.
elaine: postmortem actions: 1) revert sampling heuristic change in batching-config-v2 and re-evaluate (marcus) 2) add tenant-detection circuit to rateengine to auto-throttle extreme short-seq bursts (tom) 3) refine kernel selector telemetry to include batch size histogram (nina) 4) contact acme-analytics about traffic pattern (elaine).
marcus: short-term: create a canary test that simulates high QPS short-seq traffic and run both kernels to quantify cost & latency. I’ll start the test and share results.
elaine: p95/p99 back to baseline for hosted: p95 ~160ms, p99 ~340ms at 09:30. Closing immediate incident but keeping action items. :white_check_mark:
elaine: tagging follow-up board: https://phabricator.redwood.example/T-6579
marcus: thanks everyone. If anything re-flares ping this thread.
elaine: thanks — assigning postmortem owner to marcus and follow-ups to owners above.
